note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Geometric heterogeneity (negative, client-varying curvature) motivates tailored Lorentz spaces and time/space parameter decoupling, then results

nodes.name: Graph FL heterogeneity
nodes.description: Graph federated learning faces pronounced structural heterogeneity because clients hold structurally diverse graphs, and federated learning may even underperform local training.

nodes.name: Existing PFL is Euclidean
nodes.description: Existing personalized federated graph learning methods are confined to Euclidean space, assume uniform flat geometry, and need parameter disentanglement, client similarity estimation or auxiliary modules with significant computational overhead.

nodes.name: Negative and varying curvature
nodes.description: Client graphs predominantly have negative Forman-Ricci curvature (hyperbolic structure), and curvature values vary substantially across clients, indicating geometric heterogeneity beyond statistical differences.

nodes.name: Necessity of tailored curvature
nodes.description: Theorem 4.1: if client graphs have different average Ricci curvatures, the maximum minimal embedding distortion is at least (c_d/2) max|R_i - R_j|, so no single Lorentz scale K gives low distortion for all clients.

nodes.name: Time-like dimension encodes heterogeneity
nodes.description: Theorem 4.3: the space-like direction is independent of client identity, I(u;C)=0, while the time-like coordinate x_t has positive mutual information with client identity if its distributions differ across K.

nodes.name: Lorentz model fits parameter decoupling
nodes.description: The Lorentz model's time-space decomposition supports parameter decoupling, its linear-algebraic isometries keep aggregated parameters on the manifold, and its exponential map gives closed-form curvature-aware gradients.

nodes.name: Tailored Lorentz spaces with learnable curvature
nodes.description: FlatLand assigns each client a learnable Lorentz scale K_c (sigmoid reparameterized), initialized from its average Forman-Ricci curvature, and embeds the client's data in that space via the exponential map.

nodes.name: Parameter decoupling
nodes.description: Each Lorentz linear layer's matrix is split into a time-like column m (personalized, kept local with K_c) and a space-like block M (shared); only M is uploaded and averaged by the server as in FedAvg.

nodes.name: Correctness after aggregation
nodes.description: Proposition 6.1: applying the aggregated shared matrix still maps any vector in L^n_K to L^m_K with the same Lorentz scale, so representations remain valid hyperbolic points after aggregation.

nodes.name: Convergence and efficiency
nodes.description: Under standard FedAvg, FlatLand keeps the O(1/T) convergence rate and adds only minimal overhead such as an O(1) exponential map and curvature estimation.

nodes.name: Node classification results
nodes.description: FlatLand achieves the best or competitive accuracy in most settings, with clear gains on CiteSeer, ogbn-arxiv and Minesweeper (e.g. CiteSeer 10 clients 73.90 vs 72.35 for FED-PUB; Cora 20 clients 82.49).

nodes.name: Low-dimensional advantage
nodes.description: Reducing embedding dimension from 64 to 4 hurts hyperbolic methods much less than Euclidean ones, and FlatLand's advantage over baselines grows as dimensionality shrinks.

nodes.name: Robust to partial participation
nodes.description: On Cora with 50 clients and only 10% participation, FlatLand achieves 81.82% accuracy while FedAvg reaches only 18.14%.

nodes.name: Tailored curvature ablation
nodes.description: Fixing K=1 for all clients (w/o TS) performs worse than learning client-specific Lorentz scale parameters, which lets full FlatLand surpass the Local (L) baseline.

nodes.name: Lorentz-space decoupling ablation
nodes.description: Applying the decoupling in Euclidean space (FlatLand (E)) is clearly worse than in Lorentz space, e.g. Cora 20 clients 76.23 vs 82.49 and CiteSeer 20 clients 66.29 vs 72.24.

isolated_nodes.name: Local Lorentz often beats Euclidean
isolated_nodes.description: Local (L) often surpasses Local (E), suggesting hyperbolic space represents most datasets better, particularly heterophilic graphs.

isolated_nodes.name: Euclidean FL underperforms local training
isolated_nodes.description: Vanilla Euclidean FL baselines such as FedAvg, FedProx and FedGNN often underperform local training under strong heterogeneity.

isolated_nodes.name: FedHGCN limitations
isolated_nodes.description: FedHGCN underperforms in many heterogeneous settings because it does not model client-specific geometry, and runs out of memory on large datasets like ogbn-arxiv due to its quadratic node selection module.

isolated_nodes.name: Graph classification
isolated_nodes.description: On graph classification, FlatLand reaches 76.55 on CHEM and 67.31 on BIO-CHEM-SN, outperforming the Euclidean baselines, while Local (L) fails to beat Local (E) on multi-dataset BIO-CHEM-SN.

structural_reasoning: Argument moves from observed hyperbolic and client-varying geometry, through theory (tailored curvature, time-like heterogeneity), to the FlatLand design, correctness guarantees and experiments with ablations.
